To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we acquired dynamic volume maps in live, mechanically ventilated rats; 2) the volume maps accurately predict the pressure-volume (PV)-hysteresis; and 3) volume maps in elastase-injured rats show increased lung compliance and ventilation heterogeneities.

we acquired 4DCT of rats, and used image registration and Jacobian determinants to calculate volume changes throughout the lung during the breathing cycle, and these maps accurately predict lung PV hysterisis.
we have demonstrated for the first time the feasibility of using 4DCT to generate dynamic volume maps of rat lungs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of dynamic multiscale boundary conditions for 4DCT of healthy and emphysematous rats.
the development of a novel method for dynamic imaging of breathing rats.
the development of dynamic multiscale boundary conditions for 4DCT of live rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 4DCT imaging and registration method developed here is accurate and can be used to measure lung deformation and volume change in healthy and emphysematous rats.
we have developed a method to measure dynamic lung volume changes in rats, and we have demonstrated that these changes can be used to accurately predict the global PV hysteresisis.
we have developed, for the first-time, dynamic volume maps for use in predictive multiscale models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to acquire dynamic micro-CT images of the lungs of live rats and use them to create volume maps of the lung throughout the breathing cycles.
we developed a method for acquiring dynamic boundary conditions for multiscale modeling of lung mechanics, which we validated in healthy and emphysematous rats.

4DCT imaging of live rats allows the development of dynamic volume maps that accurately capture the lung's hysteretic PV hystereses, and that these volume maps may serve as boundary conditions for future predictive multiscale models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dynamic volume mapping can be used to predict the pressure-volume hysteresis in the lungs of rats.
we can now measure the dynamic changes in lung volume during breathing, which is critical for predictive multiscale modeling of respiration.
we developed the first dynamic volume maps from 4DCT of live rats.
